Best Family Travel Backpack: The Wayfinder 40L

By Marcus Webb · July 14, 2026

We bought this ourselves, at full price, after seeing it recommended enough times to be curious. It’s since come on three trips with us — here’s what held up and what didn’t.

Who it's for

This is a travel-day bag, not a hiking pack — the pitch is a single carry-on that works for a long-haul flight, a train transfer, and a few nights away, without checked luggage.

How it held up

Across three trips (two flights, one long train journey), the main complaint was the hip belt — adequate for redistributing weight through an airport, not something you'd want on an actual hike. Everything else about it held up well, including the zippers after regular use.

Pros and cons

What we liked

  • Opens flat like a suitcase — much easier to pack and find things than a top-loading bag
  • Dedicated padded pocket fits a laptop and a tablet separately
  • Holds its shape well even half-empty, so it doesn't sag on a luggage rack

Worth knowing

  • No built-in rain cover, which some competitors include
  • Hip belt is basic — fine for a travel day, not built for hiking

Frequently asked questions

Is the Wayfinder 40L big enough for a week away?

For one adult packing efficiently, yes — especially with packing cubes. For a family, it works well as the one 'personal item' bag carrying electronics and essentials, alongside checked or larger carry-on luggage.

Does it fit airline carry-on size limits?

It fits most major US and European carriers' carry-on dimensions, but always check your specific airline before flying, since budget carriers vary.
